title.narrative: PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE LAND AND NATURAL RESOURCE USE AT SOMUNCURA PLATEAU II

description.narrative: The purpose of this project is to support conservation efforts in the Somuncura Plateau, Patagonia, Argentina, by increasing the habitat for endangered species, reducing human wildlife conflict, and promoting ecotourism as a profitable and sustainable.activity. The Somuncura Plateau in Patagonia, Argentina, spans approximately 30,888,173 acres and sustains multiple .threatened and endemic species, including the Laguna Raimunda Frog (Atelognathus reverberii), the El Rincon Stream Frog.(Pleurodema somuncurense), the Naked Characin (Gymnocharacinus bergii), Andean Condors (Vultur gryphus), Vultures.(Cathartes aura, Coragyps atratus), Caracaras (Caracara plancus, Milvago chimango), Greater and Lesser Rheas (Rhea americana Pterocnemia pennata), Maras (Dolichotis patagonum) and Guanacos (Lama guanicoe). These species are threatened by.unsustainable livestock practices, invasive species, and human-wildlife conflict. Areas around natural freshwater sources are.trampled, contaminated, and over-grazed by livestock; aquatic vertebrates are decimated by invasive rainbow trout; and farmers.illegally hunt and poison native predators. Specific activities include: 1) sustainable management of water sources, specifically.protecting them from livestock trampling and overgrazing; 2) controlling destructive invasive species; 3) introducing shepherd.dogs to mitigate human-wildlife conflict related to predators and livestock; 4) reduceing illegal hunting and the use of poisons against predators; and the 5) promoting ecotourism as an alternative and sustainable activity. Proposed activities build on past.collaboration and participation of local stakeholders and decision-makers with support from USFWS.
